facts.t: An American Cabinet Secretary must resign from Congress to serve
facts.d: The Incompatibility Clause bars any person holding federal office from sitting in either House. In India the reverse is true — ministers must be legislators, or become one within six months. The two systems are mirror images on this point.

facts.t: The American executive cannot introduce a bill
facts.d: Every bill in Congress must be introduced by a member. The President's legislative programme has to be carried in by a sympathetic legislator — which is why the annual State of the Union address matters so much as a signalling device.

facts.t: Anti-defection is why Indian party discipline is absolute
facts.d: American legislators cross party lines routinely and pay no legal price. The Tenth Schedule makes the same act a ground for disqualification in India, which is why floor rebellions here end careers rather than merely bills.

bank.q: Comparing the two systems, consider the following statements:
s: India has a dual executive with a nominal and a real head.
In the United States the President is both head of state and head of government.
In both systems the executive is drawn from the legislature.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The American executive is separate from Congress — members of the Cabinet cannot sit in either House.

bank.q: The Indian Prime Minister's tenure depends on:
o: Retaining a majority in the Lok Sabha
A fixed term subject to impeachment
bank.e: There is no fixed term — the government falls whenever it loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the presidential system?
o: Cabinet accountable only to the President
bank.e: There is no no-confidence mechanism in a presidential system — removal is by impeachment alone, which is deliberately slow and rigorous.

bank.as: The presidential system offers greater stability but carries a risk of gridlock.
bank.rs: A fixed-term executive cannot be removed for policy disagreement, but may face a legislature controlled by the opposing party.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The parliamentary system trades that stability for the ability to change governments quickly.

bank.q: Match List I (feature) with List II (system):
pairs: 1. Loose party discipline with frequent cross-voting
2. Statutory emergency powers under the National Emergencies Act
4. Strict party discipline enforced by disqualification
bank.e: Article 75(3) provides collective responsibility, the Tenth Schedule enforces discipline, Congress is loosely disciplined, and American emergency power is statutory.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about law-making:
s: In India the executive initiates most legislation.
In the United States only members of Congress may introduce bills.
Indian ordinances under Article 123 are issued on Cabinet advice.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they show how much more legislative initiative the Indian executive holds.

bank.q: All of the following countries follow a broadly parliamentary model EXCEPT:
bank.e: Brazil is presidential, alongside Mexico, the Philippines and Nigeria.

bank.q: Which of the following is the principal cost of the parliamentary system as identified here?
o: Lower stability arising from coalitions and no-confidence votes
Inability of the executive to initiate legislation
bank.e: Accountability is its chief virtue; instability is the price. The presidential system inverts both.

bank.q: With reference to removal of the executive, consider the following statements:
s: An Indian government may be removed by a no-confidence motion at any time.
An American President may be removed only through impeachment.
Impeachment in the United States requires charges by the Senate and trial by the House.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 reverses the roles — the House brings charges and the Senate conducts the trial.

bank.q: Judicial review in the United States traces to:
bank.e: Marbury v. Madison, 1803 — the American counterpart to the way India's basic structure doctrine emerged from Kesavananda rather than from text.
